mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces expected equity discount rates, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat when trigger is active, or FEDFUNDS remains below 5.25% for the next 60 days without reversal.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (indirect via HOUST) weakens consumer demand, producing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% from previous month and HOUST decreases by >2% from previous month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when both indicators move as predicted, or wage growth outpaces unemployment increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail sales (GDPC1) exceeding 10% in a quarter predicts stronger near-term consumer confidence and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >10% from prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or flat when GDPC1 exceeds threshold, or other demand indicators (e.g., CPIAUCSL) contradict the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 3% for three consecutive months indicates softening supply constraints, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >3% each of the previous 3 months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive during the trigger, or INDPRO recovers without a lag.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% (UNRATE) for two consecutive months in a tightening regime, S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days are expected to be positive due to reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and remains below for 2 consecutive months in a tightening regime
failure_condition: Forward returns are negative when trigger occurs, or macro context is expansionary.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) followed by a decline in job openings (not directly observable but implied by context) suggests a cooling labor market, producing negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >15% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during the spike, or other labor indicators (e.g., employment growth) contradict the signal.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price indexes (CPIAUCSL) above 3% indicate accelerating inflation, which typically precedes negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when CPIAUCSL is above threshold, or other inflation measures (not available) show lower rates.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) of 5% or more for 4 consecutive months predicts supply-side softness and negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >5% over 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during the contraction, or RSAFS recovers before 4 months elapse.
